title: Somatic mutations in CTCF zinc fingers produce cellular phenotypes explained by structure-function relationships
authors: Bailey CG; Gupta S; Metierre C; Amarasekera PM; O’Young P; Kyaw W; Laletin T; Francis H; Semaan C; Singh KP; Mullighan CG; Wolkenhauer O; Schmitz U; Rasko JE
one_liner_zh: 该文结合癌症体细胞突变数据、功能实验与分子动力学模拟，系统解析CTCF锌指结构域突变对TF-DNA结合及肿瘤抑制功能的影响，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作机制的结构-功能关系，与本课题高度匹配。
abstract:
Background

Human cancers commonly contain mutations in transcription factors that lead to aberrant DNA binding or altered effector function at target sites. One such factor significantly mutated in cancer is the evolutionarily-conserved CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF), which has fundamental roles in maintaining chromatin architecture and transcriptional regulation. Numerous cancer genome sequencing and functional studies have revealed CTCF’s role as a haploinsufficient tumour suppressor gene. However, to date, structure-function relationships of somatic CTCF mutations have not been examined.

Methods

We collated somatic CTCF mutations from cancer genome portals and published studies to determine their nature, frequency, distribution and potential functional impact. We undertook an in-depth examination of 5 CTCF missense zinc finger (ZF) mutations occurring within key intra- and inter-ZF residues. We performed functional analyses including cell growth, colony-formation, chromatin immunoprecipitation and transcriptional reporter assays. Based on their homology, each ZF mutation was then modelled on CTCF’s ZF domain crystal structure and its structural impact analysed using molecular dynamics simulations.

Results

We observed an enrichment of somatic missense mutations occurring in the ZF region of CTCF, compared to the unstructured N- and C-termini. Functional characterisation of CTCF ZF mutations revealed a complete (L309P, R339W, R377H) or intermediate (R339Q) abrogation as well as an enhancement (G420D) of the anti-proliferative effects of CTCF. DNA binding at select sites was disrupted and transcriptional regulatory activities abrogated. In silico mutagenesis revealed that L309P had the highest mutation energy and thus most severe impact on protein stability. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that mutations in residues specifically contacting DNA bases or backbone exhibited loss of DNA binding (R339Q, R339W, R377H). Remarkably, R339Q and G420D were stabilised by the formation of new primary DNA bonds. All mutations exhibited some loss or gain of bonds at neighbouring residues, often in adjacent zinc fingers.

Conclusions

Our data confirm the significant negative impact haploinsufficient CTCF ZF mutations have on its tumour suppressor function. A spectrum of loss-, change- and gain-of-function impacts in CTCF zinc fingers are observed in cell growth regulation and gene regulatory activities. We have established that diverse cellular phenotypes in CTCF are explained by examining structure-function relationships.
abstract_zh:
背景

人类癌症通常含有转录因子的突变，这些突变导致异常的DNA结合或靶位点效应功能的改变。其中一个在癌症中显著突变的因子是进化上保守的CCCTC结合因子（CTCF），它在维持染色质结构和转录调控中具有基本作用。大量癌症基因组测序和功能研究揭示了CTCF作为单倍剂量不足的肿瘤抑制基因的作用。然而，迄今为止，体细胞CTCF突变的结构-功能关系尚未被研究。

方法

我们从癌症基因组门户网站和已发表的研究中收集了体细胞CTCF突变，以确定其性质、频率、分布和潜在功能影响。我们对发生在关键锌指内和锌指间残基的5个CTCF错义锌指（ZF）突变进行了深入检查。我们进行了功能分析，包括细胞生长、集落形成、染色质免疫沉淀和转录报告基因实验。基于同源性，每个ZF突变随后被建模在CTCF的ZF结构域晶体结构上，并使用分子动力学模拟分析其结构影响。

结果

我们观察到，与无序的N端和C端相比，体细胞错义突变在CTCF的ZF区域富集。CTCF ZF突变的功能表征显示，CTCF的抗增殖效应完全丧失（L309P、R339W、R377H）或部分丧失（R339Q），以及增强（G420D）。在选定位点的DNA结合被破坏，转录调控活性被消除。计算机模拟突变揭示L309P具有最高的突变能量，因此对蛋白质稳定性影响最严重。分子对接和分子动力学模拟确认，特异性接触DNA碱基或骨架的残基突变表现出DNA结合丧失（R339Q、R339W、R377H）。值得注意的是，R339Q和G420D通过形成新的初级DNA键而稳定。所有突变在邻近残基处均表现出一些键的丧失或获得，通常发生在相邻的锌指中。

结论

我们的数据确认了单倍剂量不足的CTCF ZF突变对其肿瘤抑制功能的显著负面影响。在细胞生长调控和基因调控活性中，观察到CTCF锌指中功能丧失、改变和获得的谱系。我们已确定，通过检查结构-功能关系可以解释CTCF中多样的细胞表型。
